designs.name: Completely randomized design
designs.engine: agricolae::design.crd
designs.use_when: Units are homogeneous (e.g., one growth chamber shelf with no gradient); few units.
designs.strength: Simplest analysis, maximum error df.
designs.tradeoff: No control of spatial or batch heterogeneity; rarely the best choice in greenhouses or fields.

designs.name: Randomized complete block design
designs.engine: agricolae::design.rcbd
designs.use_when: All treatments fit in one reasonably homogeneous block (bench, field strip, batch, day).
designs.strength: Simple and interpretable; removes block-to-block variation.
designs.tradeoff: Blocks become heterogeneous when they hold many entries (e.g., >20-30 field plots).

designs.name: Alpha-lattice (resolvable incomplete block) design
designs.engine: agricolae::design.alpha
designs.constraints: Number of treatments must equal block_size * number_of_blocks_per_rep; reps >= 2.
designs.use_when: Many genotypes (tens to hundreds) so complete blocks would be heterogeneous.
designs.strength: Controls within-replicate field heterogeneity with small incomplete blocks.
designs.tradeoff: Requires mixed-model analysis; block size must divide the number of entries.

designs.name: Split-plot design (whole plots in RCBD)
designs.engine: agricolae::design.split
designs.use_when: One factor is hard to randomize at small scale (irrigation, temperature chamber, tillage) and is applied to whole plots; the other factor (genotype) is randomized within them.
designs.strength: Practical for irrigation x genotype trials; precise subplot and interaction tests.
designs.tradeoff: Whole-plot factor has its own, larger error term and few df; power for it is low unless many blocks.

designs.name: Factorial treatment structure in RCBD
designs.engine: agricolae::design.ab
designs.use_when: Interest in interactions (genotype x treatment, treatment x sex) and all combinations can be randomized at the same unit level.
designs.strength: Tests main effects and interactions efficiently.
designs.tradeoff: Number of cells grows multiplicatively; interaction power needs larger n than main effects.

designs.name: Augmented block design
designs.engine: agricolae::design.dau
designs.use_when: Large number of new entries with seed for only one plot each; replicated checks estimate error and block effects.
designs.strength: Screens many unreplicated lines.
designs.tradeoff: Low precision for new entries; error df comes only from checks.

designs.name: Partially replicated (p-rep) design
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub::partially_replicated)
designs.use_when: Early-generation multi-environment trials where only a fraction of lines can be replicated.
designs.strength: More efficient than augmented designs for the same plot count.
designs.tradeoff: Needs spatial or mixed-model analysis; layout generation is non-trivial.

designs.name: Repeated-measures / longitudinal design
designs.engine: simulation only
designs.use_when: The same unit is measured over time (non-destructive phenotyping, body weight).
designs.strength: Uses within-unit correlation; models trajectories.
designs.tradeoff: Needs a correlation structure; destructive sampling over time is NOT repeated measures.

designs.name: Resolvable row-column design
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub / DiGGer); use make_design('alpha') plus add_field_coordinates() and model row and column
designs.use_when: Gradients may run in either direction (fields, greenhouse benches, chamber shelves) and replicates are contiguous rectangles.
designs.strength: Removes row and column variation within each replicate.
designs.tradeoff: Layout generation needs specialist software; analysis needs a mixed model.

designs.name: Spatial analysis of a gridded trial (SpATS / AR1xAR1)
designs.engine: analysis only: SpATS::SpATS or asreml/sommer AR1xAR1
designs.use_when: Any field or bench trial laid out on a row x column grid; especially large or low-input trials.
designs.strength: Large precision gains (residual variance -49% for sorghum yield in one study).
designs.tradeoff: Needs coordinates for every plot; model checking required.
designs.model: y ~ genotype + f(row, col) + (1 | row) + (1 | col)

designs.name: Systematic (diagonal) check arrangement for unreplicated entries
designs.engine: not_implemented (see FielDHub::diagonal_arrangement); approximate with make_design('augmented') + add_field_coordinates()
designs.use_when: Hundreds to thousands of unreplicated lines; checks spread evenly over the field to model spatial trend.
designs.strength: Even check coverage supports spatial adjustment.
designs.tradeoff: Checks use plots; entries still unreplicated.

designs.name: Line-source irrigation gradient
designs.engine: layout by distance from line; analysis with correlated subplots
designs.use_when: Water level is the treatment and is created by a single sprinkler line, so it cannot be randomized.
designs.strength: Many water levels from one line; cheap.
designs.tradeoff: Water level is not randomized; needs a correlation model and careful interpretation.
designs.model: y ~ genotype * irrigation * side + (1|block) + (1|block:side) + (1|block:irrigation), Toeplitz along distance

designs.name: Augmented-by-tray design (checks in every tray, guard edges)
designs.engine: studyforge::make_tray_design
designs.use_when: Many genotypes in seedling trays or flats (chamber or greenhouse) with too few seeds or cells for full replication.
designs.strength: Tray effects estimated from repeated checks; entries need not be replicated.
designs.tradeoff: Entries compared with low precision; checks use cells.
designs.model: y ~ check_or_entry + (1 | tray) (+ cell row/col if needed)

designs.name: Between-chamber treatments with replicated chambers or runs
designs.engine: studyforge::make_design('rcbd') with run as block and chamber as unit
designs.use_when: Temperature, CO2, light or photoperiod treatments that are set per chamber.
designs.strength: Separates treatment from chamber identity.
designs.tradeoff: Needs >=2 chambers per level or repeated runs swapping assignments; few df.

designs.name: Drosophila vial lifespan design with rearing-bottle blocks
designs.engine: studyforge::make_vial_allocation
designs.use_when: Lifespan, fecundity or survival assays in vials.
designs.strength: Each rearing bottle supplies every treatment, so rearing effects are blocked.
designs.tradeoff: Many vials to transfer; vial is the unit for food/drug treatments.

designs.name: Diallel mating design (Griffing methods 1-4)
designs.engine: cross list: all pairs (+/- reciprocals, selfs); field test in alpha/RCBD
designs.use_when: Estimate general and specific combining ability (GCA/SCA) among a modest number of parents (about 5-12).
designs.strength: Every parent combination; separates additive (GCA) and non-additive (SCA) effects.
designs.tradeoff: Crosses grow as p(p-1)/2; reciprocals double it; usually limited to fixed parents.
designs.model: y ~ GCA_i + GCA_j + SCA_ij + env + rep(env)

designs.name: North Carolina designs (NC I, NC II)
designs.engine: cross list + hierarchical (NC I) or factorial males x females (NC II)
designs.use_when: Estimate additive and dominance variance with more parents than a diallel allows; NC II for heterotic groups (males x females).
designs.strength: Scales to many parents; NC II gives GCA for both sexes/groups.
designs.tradeoff: Needs controlled pollination; many crosses to test across environments.

designs.name: Biparental / multiparental mapping population (F2, RIL, NAM, MAGIC)
designs.engine: population plan + field design (alpha) for phenotyping
designs.use_when: QTL mapping or combined linkage-association mapping.
designs.strength: Known pedigree; NAM combines linkage power with association resolution.
designs.tradeoff: Years of selfing; segregation distortion and residual heterozygosity.

designs.name: Multi-environment trial with factor-analytic GxE model
designs.engine: make_design('alpha') per environment + mixed model FA(k)
designs.use_when: Same entries in several locations/years; interest in stability and GxE.
designs.strength: Models environment-specific variances and genetic correlations.
designs.tradeoff: Needs enough environments (>= 5-6) for FA structures; complex fitting.

designs.name: Controlled-environment screen validated in the field
designs.engine: greenhouse RCBD/alpha + field MET on overlapping and independent genotypes
designs.use_when: A cheap early greenhouse trait is proposed to predict field performance.
designs.strength: Tests transferability directly.
designs.tradeoff: Pot conditions differ from field; small genotype sets give unstable correlations.
designs.model: cor(BLUP_gh, BLUP_field) with CI; or bivariate mixed model

designs.name: GWAS + expression (eQTL/TWAS/colocalization) on one diversity panel
designs.engine: panel phenotyping (alpha/MET) + RNA-seq of one tissue/time per genotype
designs.use_when: Link trait associations to genes via expression.
designs.strength: Prioritises causal genes; colocalization tests a shared variant.
designs.tradeoff: Expression is tissue/time specific; needs hundreds of genotypes for eQTL power.
designs.model: GWAS: y ~ SNP + Q + (1|K); eQTL per gene; coloc / TWAS

designs.name: Ribo-seq with matched RNA-seq
designs.engine: crd/rcbd on conditions; split each lysate into footprint and mRNA libraries
designs.use_when: Translation efficiency or translational regulation between conditions.
designs.strength: Separates transcriptional from translational change.
designs.tradeoff: Low input yields, rRNA contamination, arrest artifacts.

designs.name: Replicated ATAC-seq (with matched RNA-seq)
designs.engine: rcbd with nuclei-prep day as block
designs.use_when: Differential chromatin accessibility or regulatory region discovery.
designs.strength: Maps accessible regions with low input.
designs.tradeoff: Organellar reads in plants; Tn5 bias; needs IDR-reproducible peaks.
designs.model: counts ~ condition + prep_day (DESeq2/edgeR on consensus peaks)

designs.name: Two-organism functional validation
designs.engine: per organism: rcbd/crd with independent alleles and sibling controls
designs.use_when: Confirm a candidate gene's function in the crop and a model organism (e.g., sorghum + Arabidopsis, or mouse + fly).
designs.strength: Two independent systems make an artefact unlikely.
designs.tradeoff: Orthologs may differ in function; transformation is slow in many crops.
